abstract: General-purpose self-supervised speech encoders provide strong acoustic representations, but their pretraining objectives are not explicitly aligned with the visible articulatory dynamics required by speech-driven 3D facial animation. We propose CASE (Complementary Articulation-aware Speech Encoder), a complementary speech encoder adapted by contrastively aligning short speech clips with continuous 3D lip-mesh VQ-VAE latents. After adaptation, the geometry branch is removed, and the audio-only CASE representation is fused with the baseline SSL speech representation through residual cross-attention, while retaining the motion-decoder architecture and objective. Across four VOCASET baselines, CASE reduces mean lip vertex error by 2.8-6.0%, and mean full-face vertex error decreases in every system. Under the same fusion protocol, CASE yields lower mean LVE than the unadapted AV-SE stream on all four generators, with model-dependent margins. Because adaptation uses Korean speech-geometry pairs and evaluation uses English VOCASET, the result is consistent with cross-language downstream transfer under a shared English-pretrained audio-visual prior.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对通用语音编码器缺少可见发音几何约束的问题，CASE 用韩语语音-唇部网格对做短片段对比适配，再以残差交叉注意力把纯音频互补特征注入四种原有动画生成器，在英文 VOCASET 上把唇部顶点误差平均降低 2.8-6.0%，代价是增加约 132-135 MB 显存和额外端到端延迟。
